elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 as rendered reads "Vendor will be Customer's non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term." The "sole and exclusive" language is gone, and Section 12.3 (retained) confirms "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment" and leaves Customer free to engage any supplier.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity obligation remains after the edit, so there is no exclusivity requiring a category limit. The fallback is subsumed by the stronger preferred outcome.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the appointment is now non-exclusive, so no exclusivity period exists to cap at 12 months.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no exclusivity obligation remaining, no performance-based exit from exclusivity is needed.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity obligation remains, so no delivery-date exit trigger is required.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single element is met by replacing "sole and exclusive" with "non-exclusive" in Section 2.2, leaving no requirements or sole-supplier obligation on Customer anywhere in the cited language.

Minimality holds: only the two words creating the exclusivity were changed; Vendor remains an appointed provider, the term reference and the rest of Section 2.2 survive, and Section 12.3 is retained verbatim with no added survival tails, procedures, or extra requirements.

Intent preserved: the edit removes the internal conflict with Section 12.3 rather than creating one; the take-or-pay minimum volume in Section 2.1 is untouched and handled under its own rule, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.
The margin comment correctly cites the preferred position and offers the category/12-month/performance-exit fallback without importing any of it into the operative text.
